tool_summary: Controls the systemd system and service manager: starting, stopping, enabling, disabling, and inspecting services and units.
platform_notes: systemctl is specific to systemd-based Linux distributions. This ruleset targets Linux only.

rules.description: The mask subcommand prevents a unit from being started at all, including manually, until unmasked. disable prevents automatic start at boot. Either can silently take a service offline in a way that outlasts the current session.
The stop and restart subcommands immediately affect a running service's availability, which can disrupt dependent processes or connections.

Controls the state or configuration of system services. Known read-only subcommands (status, list-units, is-active) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future systemctl subcommands fall through to this rule; systemd's CLI surface has grown new verbs across releases, so an unmatched subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
